faq.q: Does the Sun move across the sky?
faq.a: It only seems to. The Sun stays put while the Earth spins once a day, carrying us along, so the Sun appears to travel from east to west.
asks: Is it the Sun or the Earth that moves?

faq.q: Why does the Sun rise in the east?
faq.a: The Earth spins from west to east. So each morning your part of the Earth turns towards the Sun from the east side first, and the Sun appears on the eastern horizon.
It is night when your side of the spinning Earth faces away from the Sun. At the same time, it is day on the other side of the world.
asks: Why do we have day and night?

faq.q: Why do we not feel the Earth spinning?
faq.a: The Earth spins smoothly and steadily, and everything around us, including the air, moves with us, so there is nothing to make us feel it.
asks: Why can we not feel Earth turning?

faq.q: How long does the Earth take to spin once?
faq.a: About 24 hours, which is one day. Over a year, it also travels once around the Sun.
asks: How long is one spin of the Earth?

facts: The Earth rotates once about every 24 hours, from west to east.
At the equator, the Earth's surface moves at about 1670 km/h because of its rotation.
